evidence: M-O s.v. form (document with blanks to fill in), citing Egger
terms.comment: Classically a set form of words: the formula of a lawsuit or a contract, and a register, as the list of Rome’s allies (in sociōrum fōrmulam referre, Liv. 43.6.10, Lewis & Short). Egger gives it the sense of a form with blanks to fill in.

terms.gloss: a form, a printed sheet to fill in
evidence: M-O s.v. form (document with blanks to fill in)
terms.comment: Classically scheda or scida is a sheet of paper or papyrus (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens marks the phrase as modern.

formula.html: The diminutive of fōrma, whose o de Vaan prints long and explains as lengthened before r and a consonant (pp. 233–234, s.v. fōrma); the diminutive has the same r and m. De Vaan leaves the derivatives unmarked.

sources: Lewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: scida
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. form (document with blanks to fill in).
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), pp. 233–234.
